body:
I tried looking into implementing this with a corresponding test,
 saw https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12303 seems to be superset of these changes. I have written a WPT for this here: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/63223 since it did not seem covered
 
I did also notice trying to implement that step 2 of the https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps takes parentDoc from document's container document, which is null until document is active, and for example with "create a new browsing context and document" that document is not active by that stage (so ends up being null unintentionally). I think this could be fixed by passing parentDoc as a parameter

Claude summary of that:

> Step 2 of the [internal ancestor origin objects list creation steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#internal-ancestor-origin-objects-list-creation-steps) sets parentDoc to document's container document. That goes through document's node navigable, which is null until document becomes some navigable's active document.
> 
> Both callers run before that happens:
> 
> [create a new browsing context and document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#creating-a-new-browsing-context), step 17
> [initialize the document object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#initialise-the-document-object), step 11
> 
> So parentDoc is always null, and every document's location.ancestorOrigins is empty. That contradicts browsers and WPT, for example location-ancestor-origins-new-object.html. This came from #12071.
> 
> Suggested fix: pass parentDoc in from the callers. That would be the embedder's node document for the initial about:blank, and navigationParams's navigable's container document otherwise. Step 6's unused container (#12566) has the same problem, so it can't serve as the fix.

Comment by Claude:

> Closing in favor of #12303, which makes the same fix (now rebased and marked as fixing #12563). Thanks @shannonbooth for the test; it's linked from there. The `parentDoc` issue you raised will get its own issue.
